entities.summary: Liu Bolin is a Chinese contemporary artist who specialises in self-portraits where he is disguised to match his surroundings. He earned his Bachelor of Fine Arts from the Shandong College of Arts in 1995 and his Master of Fine Arts from the Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing in 2001. His work has been exhibited in museums around the world. Also known as "the invisible man", Liu's most popular works are from his "Hiding in the City" series, photographic works that began as performance art in 2005 in response to the artists' village in which he worked in Beijing being demolished in preparation for the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Liu Bolin's 'Hiding in the City' series responded to the demolition of his artist village in Beijing, highlighting the impact of urbanization on artists and creative spaces. His work has contributed to a broader discussion about the role of art in urban development.
